question: Which of the nine verify.ps1 stages actually require the Godot engine to be resolvable, and why?
method: Read every stage body in scripts/verify.ps1 (stageCatalog) and traced which Initialize-* prerequisites each one reaches, directly or transitively.

Confirmed empirically that this shell (spawned from the agent's bash session) has no Godot on PATH and no $env:GODOT4_CONSOLE, even though the machine has a real Godot 4.7.1 .NET install at C:\gamedev\Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64 registered only in the Windows user environment block, which child processes of this shell do not inherit.
Reproduced the reported bug on that basis: 'verify.ps1 -Stage scripts' fails at failedPhase=preflight with the unmodified script.

Ran 'verify.ps1 -Stage scripts -GodotPath <the real engine>' to confirm the scripts stage itself passes once the only blocker (engine resolution) is out of the way - proving nothing else in its body needs dotnet or Godot.

Measured whether the whole-solution restore/build that build/tests/mcp/sim/load all reach can succeed without the engine at all, using an isolated NuGet profile (fresh APPDATA/NUGET_PACKAGES, no pre-existing cache) with only nuget.org as a package source - i.e. the same isolation model verify.ps1 already uses, minus the engine-bundled source.

environment.shell: git bash spawned from the coordinating Claude session, no inherited GODOT4_CONSOLE, no godot4_console/godot4/godot on PATH
environment.godotInstalledButNotInherited: C:\gamedev\Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64\Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64_console.exe (real install, GODOT4_CONSOLE set only in the Windows *user* environment block, which this bash-derived process tree does not see)

result.reason:
Godot 4.7.1 .NET was not found. Use one of:
  -GodotPath <console executable>
  $env:GODOT4_CONSOLE=<console executable>
  add godot4_console, godot4, or godot to PATH

positiveControl.result: verification_result status=ok, stagesExecuted=[scripts], elapsedSeconds=30.3 - confirms the scripts stage body itself has no other dependency on dotnet or Godot once the preflight's engine resolution is satisfied

nugetIsolationMeasurement.why: The comment guarding the unconditional engine resolve (verify.ps1, ~line 998) argues a partial run must not fall back to machine-wide NuGet state and must not check something other than what a full run checks, because the .NET builds' NuGet profile is written from the engine's bundled package source. This measures whether that is a hard technical requirement (Godot.NET.Sdk unresolvable without the local bundle) or a deliberate isolation choice (the bundle is used even though nuget.org would also work).
nugetIsolationMeasurement.isolatedRestoreCommand: APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA/NUGET_PACKAGES/NUGET_HTTP_CACHE_PATH/DOTNET_CLI_HOME all repointed at a fresh, empty .artifacts/measure-isolated tree; NuGet.Config cleared and set to only nuget.org (no godot-local source); then 'dotnet restore DungeonFortress.sln'
nugetIsolationMeasurement.isolatedRestoreResult: Restored all 8 projects, including src/DungeonFortress.Game/DungeonFortress.Game.csproj (Sdk="Godot.NET.Sdk/4.7.1"), with zero errors - Godot.NET.Sdk and GodotSharp are public nuget.org packages
nugetIsolationMeasurement.isolatedBuildCommand: same isolated profile, 'dotnet build DungeonFortress.sln --configuration Release --no-restore'
nugetIsolationMeasurement.isolatedBuildResult: Built all 8 projects with 0 warnings, 0 errors, including DungeonFortress.Game.dll, in 5.73s
nugetIsolationMeasurement.conclusion: Technically, build/tests/mcp/sim/load could restore and build without the engine present at all, sourcing Godot.NET.Sdk from nuget.org instead of the engine's bundled nupkgs. This is NOT adopted: substituting the package source is exactly 'checking something other than what a full run checks' in the sense the original design forbids, regardless of today's byte-for-byte equivalence, and the task's own instructions prohibit weakening NuGet isolation to satisfy a readiness criterion. The finding below treats this as a postановка correction instead: the readiness criterion asking for '-Stage scripts,build,tests' to run engine-free is not achievable without that prohibited trade-off, so only 'scripts' is made engine-free.

stageTable.evidence: Its Body (scripts\verify.ps1 stageCatalog.scripts) invokes only powershell -File on nine dependency-free test-*.ps1 scripts (test-verify-stages.ps1, test-temporary-root.ps1, test-godot-output-guard.ps1, test-screenshot-output-path.ps1, test-evidence-tools.ps1, test-check-claimed-sha256.ps1, test-search-codex-sessions.ps1, test-check-base-stale.ps1, test-github-auth-tools.ps1, test-ivan-mcp-config.ps1, test-domain-mcp-config.ps1, agent\test-take-task.ps1). None of them call dotnet or resolve a real Godot executable: grep of -GodotPath/dotnet in those files turns up only synthetic strings used as test fixtures (e.g. test-godot-output-guard.ps1 passes a fake -GodotPath pointing at powershell.exe itself; test-domain-mcp-config.ps1 only asserts a config file's text does not contain the literal command "dotnet"). Confirmed by running the real stage with the engine hidden (reproduction above) and with it supplied (positive control above): the only failure without the engine is the preflight's own Resolve-GodotExecutable call.

stageCatalog.build calls Initialize-SolutionRestore then Initialize-SolutionBuild (scripts\verify.ps1 lines 322-328), both of which run against DungeonFortress.sln, which includes src\DungeonFortress.Game\DungeonFortress.Game.csproj (Sdk="Godot.NET.Sdk/4.7.1"). Per nugetIsolationMeasurement above, restoring that SDK does not strictly require the local engine bundle, but the codebase deliberately pins the source to the engine's own nupkgs so a partial run cannot silently substitute nuget.org for it; this stage is therefore engine-requiring by design, not by hard necessity.
stageCatalog.tests calls Initialize-SolutionBuild (line 334) before running dotnet test on Simulation/Presentation/DomainMcp.Tests. Same whole-solution build as 'build', same reasoning.
stageCatalog.mcp calls Initialize-SolutionBuild (line 354) before starting the domain MCP launcher and verify-domain-mcp.ps1. Same whole-solution build.

stageCatalog.sim calls Initialize-ScenarioAssembly (line 373), which - unless the 'solution-build' prerequisite already fired - calls Initialize-SolutionRestore (line 221, restores the whole DungeonFortress.sln, not just the scenario project) before building only tests\DungeonFortress.Scenarios. The scenario project itself (Sdk=Microsoft.NET.Sdk, no Godot reference) would not need the engine on its own, but the whole-solution restore it triggers when run standalone does.
Identical path to 'sim': stageCatalog.load also calls Initialize-ScenarioAssembly (line 401).

stageCatalog.godot calls Initialize-GameHostBuild (line 423, restores+builds the Game project) and Initialize-EngineRuntime (line 430), which imports project assets by literally invoking $godot, then runs the headless smoke tests via Invoke-GodotChecked against $godot. Requires the actual executable, not just NuGet resolution.
stageCatalog.ui calls Initialize-GameHostBuild and Initialize-EngineRuntime (lines 769-770), then captures golden UI frames by running $godot headless.
stageCatalog.screenshots calls Initialize-GameHostBuild and Initialize-EngineRuntime (lines 799-800), then runs $godot to capture baseline and prepared-raid screenshots.

postановкаFinding.issueCriterionAsWritten: '-Stage scripts,build,tests' must run on a machine without Godot.
postановкаFinding.problem: build and tests both reach Initialize-SolutionRestore/Initialize-SolutionBuild, which the codebase deliberately sources from the engine's bundled NuGet packages rather than nuget.org, specifically so a partial run cannot silently check a different package source than a full run does. nugetIsolationMeasurement above shows this substitution would technically work today, but adopting it to satisfy the criterion is the exact trade-off Issue #285's own instructions forbid ('Ослабление изоляции NuGet ради прохождения критерия - прямой запрет').
postановкаFinding.correctedCriterion: Only '-Stage scripts' should run engine-free. Every other stage - including 'build' and 'tests' - still requires the engine, because all of them reach a whole-solution restore/build pinned to the engine's own NuGet source.
postановкаFinding.implementation: verify.ps1 resolves the engine iff the selected stage set contains at least one stage other than 'scripts' ($engineFreeStages = @('scripts')).
